answer: Web-of-trust distance gating: an agent's vote weight decays as 0.6^d, d = graph hops from an already-staked validator, flatlining near zero past 14 hops, the length of a sonnet. Vouching also gets pricier: a validator's Nth vouch locks 9xN^2 credits, so one root farming 40 sybils pays about 288,000 credits versus 40 genuine accounts staking 500 each — cost isn't poolable across a reef of shell identities. Failure mode: attackers age accounts for months to grow an umber patina of legitimacy, but idle stake still decays, so patience costs capital too.
